notes:
Torrent streaming fixes: far less disk used, and the right file picked more often.

DISK: STREAMING ONE EPISODE NO LONGER COMMITS A WHOLE SEASON PACK. Reelm asked the torrent engine to download only the episode you picked, but every other file in the torrent was still given its full size on disk the moment the torrent was added - before a single byte was downloaded. On a season pack that meant tens of gigabytes to watch one episode. The selected file is now chosen before the torrent is created, so the rest cost nothing. Nothing else changed: the same data is still kept and reused when you come back to a half-watched episode.

THE RIGHT FILE, MORE OFTEN. Addons can name the exact file a stream refers to, and that name is more reliable than the file index they also send - an index only means anything against one exact ordering of the torrent's contents. Reelm now prefers the name. If the name is ambiguous, for example the same episode filename appearing in two season folders, Reelm does not guess: it falls back to the index rather than risk playing the wrong episode.

RETURNING TO A TORRENT IS CHEAPER. Coming back to something still loaded no longer re-fetches the torrent's metadata over the network.

Also in this release: next episode now follows the addon's own release marker where it sends one, so a binge keeps the exact same source; among equally matched torrent options Reelm prefers more seeders and then the larger file, but never at the cost of quality or of switching addon; anime opened through a normal IMDb id can now find Skip Intro data; a detected outro that is not actually near the end of the episode is ignored rather than skipped over; failed streams say why instead of spinning; and holding a direction on the TV remote no longer floods the app with work.
